messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: elevated 5xx + latency observed in Hosted API and multiple Dedicated pools in eu-west-1. Error spike correlates with STS/auth egress failures and outbound observability timeouts. Auto-routing triggered. Paging on-call.

anya: oncall here, seeing 5xx rate jump ~12:03 UTC, p50 latency doubled for short queries. Hosted API 5xx mainly 502/504, Dedicated pools seeing increased request timeouts. Digging into auth failures now.

mike: adding logs — from edge proxy: `503 upstream connect error or timeout` and intermittent `x-aws-sts: 500` responses from eu-west-1 STS endpoints. Also heavy retry storms from sidecars.

priya: @anya do we have a routing fallback in place for auth failures? We can route to eu-west-2 if STS in eu-west-1 is degraded, but need to ensure token caches/issuance cross-region works for Dedicated pools.

anya: yes we have cross-region fallback but it's opt-in per pool. I'm going to enable region-fallback policy for Hosted API and non-sensitive Dedicated pools. Doing in config now.

ops-bot: running rollout: `redwoodctl routing update --scope hosted,dpools --policy cross-region-fallback --to eu-west-2` (started)

bennett: hold on on the full switch — token issuance uses instance profile flows that are regional. For Dedicated pools with strict VPC egress, fallback could fail. I'll annotate pools that should be excluded.

priya: good call. @bennett list the pool IDs you want excluded and I'll exclude them from auto-failover.

bennett: excluded: dp-58c9, dp-612a, dp-6f31. Proceed with enabling for the rest.

mike: posting quick snippet of the spike timeline:
```
12:03:01 UTC - first auth 500s
12:03:12 UTC - edge proxies report increasing upstream timeouts
12:03:45 UTC - Hosted API 5xx crosses 3% threshold
12:04:10 UTC - Routing fallback auto-policy triggered
12:05:00 UTC - retries amplified traffic to observability ingestion
12:06:15 UTC - we start seeing observability timeouts (otel collector)
```

support: customer impact: support queue shows multiple reports of timeouts/slow responses for EU customers. No billing impact reported but some requests failed. We're preparing status page draft.

status-team: drafting. Proposed status update: "Investigating elevated errors and latency in eu-west-1 affecting API requests and some Dedicated customers. Mitigations in progress, updates every 15 minutes." Any objections? :hourglass_flowing_sand:

priya: no objections. Please include the note about optional Dedicated pools excluded from cross-region failover.

incident-bot: NOTE: Alert correlation suggests root cause likely: aws-sts regional control plane egress failures combined with increased outgoing traffic to observability (ingestion) causing backpressure and amplified retries.

anya: immediate mitigation plan I'm executing now:
- enable cross-region routing fallback for Hosted API + most Dedicated pools
- apply aggressive retry backoff on edge (reduce client retries, set jitter)
- temporarily reduce observability ingestion throughput (throttle) to relieve egress
- open AWS support case and request STS/EC2 egress health check
- update status page and coordinate customer comms

mike: commands I'm running:
```
# reduce retries at edge
kubectl -n edge patch configmap edge-retries --patch '{"data":{"max_retries":"1","base_backoff_ms":"200","max_backoff_ms":"1000"}}'

# throttle obliv collector
kubectl -n observability patch deploy otel-collector --patch '{"spec":{"replicas":1}}'
```

bennett: I've started a script to clear hot token caches and warm cross-region caches so new tokens are issued from eu-west-2 where available. Script run id: warm-202704.

support: customers flagged as possibly impacted: acme-inc, edu-spark, shopora. Reaching out to top-tier customers with initial note: ETA 30m for next update.

aws-support: AWS case opened: 9876543210. We see STS control plane errors in eu-west-1, ENG is investigating internal routing. AWS advised to use cross-region endpoints as workaround while they triage.

priya: quick check — do we have any dedicated pools pinned to specific AMIs or subnets that block cross-region STS? @bennett

bennett: three pools pinned, already excluded. Others are fine.

anya: update: routing fallback completed for Hosted API and 8/11 Dedicated pools. Observability throttling applied. Early metrics show 5xx rate reducing from 3.2% -> 1.1% within 5 mins.

mike: seeing decreased p50/p90 now. Still occasional spikes when retries from older clients hit old region. Might need to invalidate client-side cached metadata.

priya: can we push a header that forces token refresh for edge clients? Eg add `x-redwood-force-sts-refresh: 1` for new sessions.

anya: yes deploying edge header rewrite now.

ops-bot: rollout: `redwoodctl edge config apply --patch 'force_sts_refresh=true'` (completed)

support: status page updated and posted at https://status.redwood.example/incidents/2478123456 — initial notice and next update at 15:30 UTC.

status-team: posted. Customers notified via email and in-app banners for affected orgs.

mike: continuing to watch traces; observability sampling reduced so traces sparse but latency dims improving.

bennett: AWS says they've implemented a fix on their side for the STS edge, waiting for propagation. They recommend keeping fallback until 1 hour after their fix is globally observed.

anya: plan for next hour: keep fallback for Hosted + eligible Dedicated pools, keep observability throttled, monitor 5xx and latency, coordinate with support for customer updates. If stable for 30m, begin staged rollback of fallbacks (except excluded pools).

priya: handoff in 20 minutes to @mike for overnight monitoring. Mike take over when ready.

mike: taking handoff in 20. I'll post final state and runbook steps in 15.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: PAGER HANDOFF scheduled — from anya to mike at 12:40 UTC. If any escalation, page SRE lead.

anya: leaving notes:
- root cause likely external (AWS STS egress). Non-root mitigations: region-fallback, token cache warm, reduce edge retries, throttle observability.
- pools excluded: dp-58c9, dp-612a, dp-6f31
- AWS case: 9876543210
- follow metrics: hosted_api/5xx_rate, dedicated_pool/*/timeouts, obs/ingest/errors

mike: confirmed. I'll continue monitoring dashboards and escalate if 5xx >1.5% for >10m.

support: sent follow-up to impacted customers with workaround (retry with backoff and note about transient auth errors). No escalations yet.

aws-support: AWS update: propagation looks healthy in eu-west-1 — recommend keeping fallback for 30 more minutes, then test rollback on a small subset.

mike: okay starting a canary rollback for Hosted API only in 30m, will monitor for 10m before wider rollback.

priya: thanks everyone. Great coordination. Adding short postmortem template in this thread for follow-up items (observability throttling playbook, automations for token cache warming, better detection rules for STS region failures).

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (monitoring): primary mitigations successful; on-call handoff complete. Please fill out post-incident form: /incidents/2478123456/postmortem when ready. :white_check_mark:"
